newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS downgrades Canadian Occidental debt.
newsitem.headline: CBRS downgrades Canadian Occidental debt.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday it lowered its ratings of Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd's short and long-term debt while maintaining a stable outlook for the securities.
CBRS said it cut its rating of CanOxy's short-term debt to A-1 (low) from A-1 and long-term debt to A (low) from A.
The bond rating service placed the securities on credit watch in March after CanOxy announced its friendly, C$2 billion cash takeover bid for Wascana Energy Inc.
CanOxy was successful in acquiring 87.8 percent of Wascana shares by the bid deadline of April 14.

CBRS said it maintained a prime quality rating on the company's C$300 million commercial paper program and good quality rating on its debentures because of an enhanced land position and reserve profile, domestic and international operations diversity and strong cash flow from its chemicals arm.
However, the high lebt load assumed to finance the Wascana buy and relative weakness in oil and natural gas prices that could extend "beyond the current phase" were offsetting factors.
CanOxy arranged a C$1.8 billion unsecured credit line to acquire Wascana and its net debt will increase by about C$2 billion from the year end 1996 level, CBRS said.
CBRS said it remained confident that CanOxy's management would restore the required balance in its capital structure during the next two years.
